A.explanation: Side $x$ joins V to W but it is not perpendicular to the forces, so $Fx$ is not the perpendicular separation.

B.explanation: The perpendicular distance between the two parallel forces is $y$, so torque is $Fy$.

C.explanation: A couple needs only one factor of $F$ times separation, so $2Fx$ double counts the two forces.

D.explanation: Although $y$ is the correct separation, a couple is $F$ times separation, not $2F$ times separation.

hints: Notice the small right-angle mark at V between force $F$ and side $y$ - what does this tell you about the force direction?
Recall torque of a couple is $F$ multiplied by the perpendicular distance between the two parallel lines of action.
Project the separation VW onto the direction parallel to side $y$ to find the perpendicular distance between the forces.
walkthrough: Identify the couple: two equal, opposite and parallel forces $F$ at V and W, so torque $= F \times$ perpendicular distance between their lines.
Use the diagram mark at V: each $F$ is perpendicular to side $y$. Therefore the perpendicular to $F$ is parallel to $y$.
The separation needed is the distance between the two force lines measured along the direction of $y$.
Points V and W are joined by side $x$, which is the hypotenuse. Its projection onto the $y$-direction equals the adjacent side $y$.
Hence perpendicular distance $= y$ and torque $= Fy$. This is option B.
